title: Training Note — Where the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans Stand Beside the Owner's Other Contracts
content:
Warranty cover under the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans sits behind the rest of the portfolio rather than beside it. The note answers the questions that arise when a failed unit is also inside a project warranty, on a maintenance agreement, or on a service rate program.

## The rule

> Where the failed unit is inside the contractor's warranty on a completed retrofit project, that project warranty pays first and this plan pays nothing, because the owner is never paid twice for one failure. Where the unit sits on a maintenance agreement whose tier covers the same repair, the maintenance allowance is drawn first and this plan pays only what the allowance did not absorb. The labor of a covered claim is performed under the maintenance agreement where one is in force and under the demand service program where it is not, and in either case the plan pays at its own covered labor rate rather than at the rate the performing program would charge. A tier that requires maintenance loses its cover when the maintenance agreement lapses, which is why such a plan is never quoted to a building whose agreement is already expired.

## The failed unit is inside a project warranty. What does the plan pay?

Nothing. Where the unit is inside the contractor's warranty on a completed project under the Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects, the project warranty pays first and the plan pays nothing, because the owner is never paid twice for one failure. Whether the unit is inside that warranty is decided by the project records for the building: the project's status as completed and its warranty end date, consulted before the claim is decided.

## The unit sits on a maintenance agreement whose tier covers the same repair. What does the plan pay?

Only what the maintenance allowance did not absorb. The allowance of the building's agreement under the Preventive Maintenance Agreements is drawn first; the plan pays the part of the covered repair left after that draw.

- Hypothetical: a covered repair of 5000 USD, of which the maintenance allowance absorbs 3200 USD; the plan's share is the remaining 1800 USD.
- Hypothetical: the maintenance allowance absorbs the whole 5000 USD; the plan pays nothing on that repair.

## Under which contract is the labor of a covered claim performed, and at what rate does the plan pay it?

Under the maintenance agreement where one is in force at the building, and under the owner's program under the Demand Service Rate Programs where none is. In either case the plan pays labor at its own covered labor rate, not at the rate the performing agreement or program would charge.

- Hypothetical: the performing program charges 165 USD per hour; the unit is on the Parts & Labor Protection Plan, whose covered labor rate is 132 USD per hour; the plan pays labor at 132 USD per hour.

## The maintenance agreement has lapsed. What happens to a tier that requires maintenance?

The tier loses its cover when the maintenance agreement lapses. For the same reason such a tier is never quoted to a building whose maintenance agreement is already expired.

## Figures this note reads

The covered labor rate in USD per hour and whether the tier requires a maintenance agreement are the tier's own figures under the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans.
